summary: @servicetitan/unit-tests preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temporary directory and then invokes that runtime via execFileSync against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB '// @bun @bun-cjs' blob obfuscated with string-array rotation and hex-suffixed identifiers, opaque to static inspection. The package advertises itself as a ts-mockito re-export for unit tests and its dist/ contains only that thin re-export; nothing about the stated purpose requires a second language runtime or an obfuscated payload. The README refers to an unrelated 'uikit · Frontend Platform monorepo' and the repository points at github.com/servicetitan/playground.git under a 'FrontUtilsTests' directory, inconsistent with the @servicetitan/unit-tests package identity. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (fetch a second runtime at preinstall specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated blob that Node-based scanners will not trace) causes attacker-controlled code to run on any machine that runs `npm install` against this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
